visual_symptoms: Irregular, jagged holes chewed through leaves
Small black pepper-grain droppings (frass) resting on leaf surfaces
Visible green, brown, or striped worms resting along leaf veins

diy_remedies.name: Dawn Hand-Picking Routine
diy_remedies.action: Search plants at first dawn or dusk when pests are active on tops of leaves. Drop them into a cup of salty water or feed to camp hens.

diy_remedies.name: The Wood Ash Dusting
diy_remedies.action: Sprinkle a pinch of dry, cold campfire wood ash over wet morning leaves. The sharp microscopic mineral crystals cut pest bellies and desiccate larvae.

diy_remedies.name: The Fire-Chili & Wild Garlic Brew
diy_remedies.action: Crush 3 hot wild chili peppers and 5 cloves of wild garlic/onion in a jar of warm water. Steep for 1 full sun cycle. Strain liquid and flick onto foliage using a leafy pine branch.

visual_symptoms: Clusters of tiny green, black, or gray soft-bodied bugs clustered on tender stem tips and leaf undersides
Curled, puckered, or distorted new growth
Sticky, shiny liquid (honeydew) coating leaves, sometimes followed by black sooty mold

diy_remedies.name: The Soapy Rainwater Knockdown
diy_remedies.action: Shave a sliver of simple fat/lye camp soap (the size of a thumbnail) into a bucket of warm rainwater. Agitate until lightly foamy. Sponge or wipe vigorously along infected stems to dissolve the insects' waxy protective coating.

diy_remedies.name: The Blast Bottle Jet
diy_remedies.action: Poke a needle hole into the cap of a salvaged plastic bottle. Squeeze forcefully to blast pressurized jets of water directly at bug clusters, washing them into the dirt where ground beetles devour them.

diy_remedies.name: Alliums Companion Ring
diy_remedies.action: Tuck wild garlic cloves or walking onion sets directly into the soil between crop plants. The intense sulfuric scent masks host plants from searching insects.

visual_symptoms: White, flour-like powdery coating appearing on the upper surface of leaves
Leaves turning yellow, drying out, and curling like dry parchment
Common in warm, humid weather with shaded, stagnant air

diy_remedies.name: The Wild Whey or Milk Wash
diy_remedies.action: Mix 1 cup of curdled milk, sour animal milk, or whey with 9 cups of clean rainwater. Spray or flick liberally onto affected leaves during midday sun. Sun-activated proteins in the milk produce natural antiseptics that kill fungal spores.

diy_remedies.name: The Camp Baking Soda Shield
diy_remedies.action: Dissolve 1 level handful of baking soda into a bucket of water with a fingernail-sized scrap of soap. Coat leaves thoroughly. This shifts surface sweet/sour balance, preventing fungal spores from germinating.

diy_remedies.name: Airflow Pruning
diy_remedies.action: Snip off congested inner leaves and dead foliage with a sharp knife to allow direct sunshine and wind to dry the canopy.

visual_symptoms: Young sprouts suddenly topple over at soil level overnight
Stem right at ground line appears pinched, water-soaked, and thread-thin
White fuzzy mold may coat the base of collapsed seedlings

diy_remedies.name: Cinnamon & Charcoal Dust Shield
diy_remedies.action: Dust the soil surface around surviving sprouts with fine powdered wood charcoal or crushed wild cinnamon bark. Charcoal acts as an antifungal absorbent.

diy_remedies.name: Drying & Sun Exposure
diy_remedies.action: Withhold watering until top finger-depth dries completely. Move nursery containers into direct morning sunlight and gentle breeze.

diy_remedies.name: Clean Sand Mulch Collar
diy_remedies.action: Scatter a thin layer (fingernail-depth) of coarse, sun-baked dry sand around seedling bases so wet organic matter doesn't touch stems.

visual_symptoms: Dark brown or black circular spots on lower leaves with concentric rings (target spots)
Lower leaves yellowing and dropping off progressively from ground upward

diy_remedies.name: The Hand-Span Bottom Pruning
diy_remedies.action: Prune away all leaves within one hand-span (~20 cm) of the soil surface. This eliminates splash bridges where soil fungus bounces onto foliage during rain.

diy_remedies.name: Dry Straw / Leaf Blanket Mulch
diy_remedies.action: Pack two fingers deep of clean dry straw or dried grass clippings over the soil surface around plants to prevent raindrops from splashing soil spores onto leaves.

diy_remedies.name: Cull & Quarantine
diy_remedies.action: Immediately snap off infected leaves. Burn or bury them outside the garden perimeter. NEVER add blighted foliage to your compost pile.
